title: C175B — Powertrain control module (PCM)
introduction:
I use this reference to connect a cavity’s position in the drawing with its circuit description in the table. Think of it as the PCM’s seating chart: neighboring terminals can have very different jobs. The PCM receives information and sends commands, so a control or monitoring connection should not be mistaken for the power feed to the device it names.

Start with the connector identity and harness information, locate the printed cavity label, then read across its assignment row. Keep the original tables beside the illustration. This is a reference for identifying connections, not an access, disconnection, probing or diagnostic procedure. Physical viewing direction, the shading legend, gauge convention and Size/Used code definitions are not supplied; leave those meanings unassigned. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the drawing’s cavity count. Some cavities have both populated and blank assignment rows without qualifiers selecting between them. These conflicts remain unresolved; this reference does not establish the physical count or which competing assignment applies to a particular vehicle.

edits.why: I use the broad housing projections at the drawing’s left and the narrow cavity group at its right as landmarks within this displayed view, without assigning release or locking functions to them. In the main field, cavity labels increase from left to right across each row, with successive rows above. The narrow right-hand group has its own printed arrangement; do not extend a main-field row into it. Locate positions by their labels rather than by counting circles or interpreting their fill.

The Cavity column links the drawing to the row. Circuit Number identifies the circuit; Color and Gauge record its wire description; Function explains its named role; Qualifier records applicability; Used and Terminal Part Number retain the remaining assignment information. Read the complete row together. Starter sensing, generator control, fuel-pump command and fuel-pump monitoring are distinct roles, even though they meet at the same controller. Likewise, a signal return and a named ground are not interchangeable labels. Conflicting populated and blank rows remain unresolved; neither a blank row nor the drawing’s shading settles them. The next useful step is to carry the identified circuit into the matching wiring or diagnostic procedure, where test conditions and expected results belong.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata declares Pin Count 107, while the attached illustration’s highest cavity label is 103. Confirm whether the count and illustration describe the same connector; additional positions cannot be inferred.

Cavities 14, 15 and 17 each have both a populated circuit assignment marked Used 1 and a blank assignment marked Used 0, with no distinguishing qualifiers. Confirm the intended applicability of these competing rows before treating either as definitive.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 127 primary units, six complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 56 units/two headings. Introduction explicitly discloses count disagreement and populated-versus-blank assignment conflicts. Other public fields remain equal to original author. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
